newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends at 3.0 pct, gilts continue rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends at 3.0 pct, gilts continue rise.

text.p: Indian call money ended down on easy availability of funds on Thursday while government securities continued their recent rise, dealers said.
They said call money ended around 3.0 percent against opening quotes of 3.5-4.0 percent.
Most of the day's trade was done around 3.25 percent, dealers said.
Demand for securities continued to be high, spurred by easy call money..
Security prices have been on the rise since the beginning of the financial year on April 1 and have been particularly steep in the last week.
"Prices rose further today...there was demand for all tenures," said one dealer at a state-run bank. "The continued rise is a bit surprising. No one is sure how much longer this will coninue."
"Four-year paper, which was traded yesterday at around 10.9 percent, yielded 10.6 today," he said.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) auctions 50 billion rupees of four-year bonds on July 28 and dealers said expecattions of the cut-off had now been revised down to 10.65-10.75 from an earlier 10.75-10.90 percent.
Among actively traded stocks, the 11.83 percent 2003 rose to 102 rupees from Wednesday's 101.54, while the 12.59 percent 2004 leapt to 105 from 104.55
The 11.75 percent 2001 moved up sharply to 103.68 from 102.70 as traders built up positions ahead of Monday's auction.
Among other stocks, the Treasury bill maturing on October 18 yielded 6.25 percent against Wednesday's 6.35.
